analysis.investment_thesis: Mastek built an impressive 9-year track record (23.3% revenue CAGR, 32.5% net profit CAGR) anchored in Oracle cloud and UK public-sector digital transformation, but recent growth has decelerated sharply to ~7% YoY — far below the 20%+ I require for a conviction growth holding. At P/E 12.8 and P/S 1.48 the market is pricing in this slowdown, leaving little margin of safety for a Fisher-style portfolio that demands growth, not cheapness.
key_strengths: 9-year revenue CAGR of 23.3% proves durable execution across multiple technology cycles
Niche Oracle Cloud + UK government positioning creates some switching-cost stickiness
Conservative balance sheet (D/E 0.20) and strong FCF generation (INR 515 Cr in FY26) provide financial resilience
key_risks: Growth deceleration is severe: revenue growth slowed to ~7% YoY (FY25→FY26), well below Fisher's 20%+ threshold
ROE at 15.6% is below my 20% minimum — insufficient return on invested capital for a premium growth valuation
UK public-sector concentration creates lumpy, budget-cycle-dependent revenue with limited pricing power
red_flags: Revenue grew only INR 244 Cr (7.1%) in FY26 vs INR 400 Cr+ additions in peak years — a structural deceleration, not a one-year blip
Finance costs spiked from INR 8 Cr (FY22) to INR 44 Cr (FY24) on acquisition debt, suggesting growth was partly bought rather than organically earned
EBITDA actually contracted in FY25 (INR 455 Cr vs INR 491 Cr in FY23), revealing margin fragility beneath the trend label
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Through my scuttlebutt lens, Mastek is a well-managed mid-tier IT services company that has executed intelligently — the Oracle Cloud and UK government niches are genuinely defensible, and the FY17–FY22 compounding from INR 560 Cr to INR 2,184 Cr in revenue is the kind of track record I admire. Management has been disciplined with capital (D/E 0.20, consistent positive OCF across all 5 observed years), and FCF conversion is actually improving (FY26 FCF of INR 515 Cr on INR 404 Cr net profit). These are marks of an honest, capable team.

However, the growth profile no longer fits what I demand. At 7% YoY revenue growth and 7% net profit growth in FY26, Mastek has slipped from a growth company into a mature compounder. My philosophy is to buy growth and hold — not to hold deceleration and hope. ROE of 15.6% and operating margin of 14.1% are adequate but not exceptional; I want to see ROE above 20% expanding over time, which this business is not delivering. The P/E of 12.8 is seductively cheap but cheap prices on slowing businesses are value traps, not opportunities. I would revisit if the company demonstrates a re-acceleration catalyst — a significant AI/automation practice win or a transformative acquisition that reignites 20%+ growth.
